---
title: "Calibration curves per chemical (4.4)"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("_prepare.R")
box::use(show = projlib/show, util = projlib/msdial_utils)
tr <- tut$to_report
# The normalization with the lowest QC RSD% (the app's default choice) and its first batch, as the
# app shows them at the start
best <- tr[["best normalization"]]
mat_id <- util$mat_id_of_blank_subtracted(best)
lst <- tut$proc[[mat_id]]
b <- names(lst)[1]
x <- lst[[b]]
```

For every targeted compound (`Quant` in the MS-DIAL comment), QuaNTA fits a calibration curve to
the calibration samples (`Cal…` classes) and uses it to turn the signal of every sample into a
concentration. Figure **4.4** of the app shows the curve of the compound selected in table **4.2**.
Below is the same figure as in the app, with the example data (batch `r b`,
`r tut$method_labels[[best]]` normalization); here, choose the compound in the list or search it by
name.

```{r}
#| label: viewer-4-4
# The viewer of the app (app/www/calcurve_viewer.js, copied to assets/ before each render) with the
# data the app sends for this batch: the batch's curves, and for compounds on the global curve also
# the calibration points of all batches; the compounds removed before calibration last
rd <- SumExp::row_df(x$calcurve)
rem <- tr[["removed features"]]
rem <- rem[rem$mat_id == best & rem$targeted, ]
rf <- tr[["qc rsd filter"]]
why <- ifelse(rem$reason == "QC RSD%", paste0("QC RSD% ", round(rem$qc_rsd, 1), "% > ", rf$max_targeted, "%"), "blank filter")
norm <- tr[["normalized"]]
removed <- if (nrow(rem) > 0) {
  show$calib_view_removed(norm, best, rem$feature_id, stats::setNames(why, rem$feature_id),
                          batch = if (b %in% as.character(SumExp::col_df(norm)$batch_id)) b)
}
views <- list()
if (length(lst) > 1) {
  views[["All batches (global curve)"]] <- list(
    parts = list(show$calib_view_all_batches(lst, b, mat_id)),
    info = paste0("Concentrations in batch ", b, " were calculated with the global curve, fitted on the ",
                  "calibration points of all batches shown here."))
}
views[[if (length(lst) > 1) paste0("Batch ", b, " only") else "All samples"]] <- list(
  parts = list(show$calib_view_of_batch(x, mat_id), removed),
  info = paste0("Only batch ", b, "'s calibration points are shown: the concentrations were calculated with the ",
                "global curve, fitted on the calibration points of all batches."),
  info_warn = TRUE)
cv_data <- show$calib_viewer_data(
  compounds = data.frame(id = c(rownames(x$calcurve), rem$feature_id), name = c(rd$feature_name, rem$feature_name)),
  views = views, log_scale = isTRUE(tr$params$log_calibration),
  unit = show$conc_unit(x$concn),
  y_title = show$label_if_has(x$concn[[util$mat_id_in_calibration(mat_id)]], "Signal"),
  class_colors = tut$class_colors
)
show$calib_viewer_html("calcurve-viewer", cv_data, script_src = "assets/calcurve_viewer.js")
```

The figure has two modes; switch with the buttons, or with the arrow keys ← and →. The arrow keys
↑ and ↓ go to the previous and next compound (in the app, the rows of table 4.2).

- **Calibration inspection** (first): every calibration point, each injection of a calibration
  sample, at its spiked (nominal) concentration and its measured signal. Points of the same
  concentration are replicates; with several batches, the symbol tells the batch. The colours tell
  the role of each level:
  - *Cal0* (red): the zero calibrant. Its signal gives the thresholds of the LOD (3×) and the LLOQ
    (10×, or the mean plus 3 / 10 standard deviations). On log axes, a concentration of 0 has no
    place: Cal0 is a short line at the left edge, at its signal.
  - *LOD* (blue): the lowest level whose mean signal is above the LOD threshold.
  - *Within limits* (green): the levels the curve is fitted on, from the LLOQ upwards.
  - *Above the ULOQ* (olive): levels in the curve but above its linear range.
  - *Out-of-range* (grey): levels not used for the curve.
- **Final calibration model**: the fitted curve, the calibration points it was fitted on (black),
  and the QCs (blue; the QC group in the hover text) and study samples (by class) at the
  concentration the curve gives them. Values replaced by the LOD/LLOQ rules are open circles; their
  hover text tells the rule and the calculated concentration.

In both modes:

- **Shading**: dark grey below the LOD, light grey below the LLOQ, and olive above the ULOQ (dashed
  line), the top of the linear range. **Labels** at the top name each limit in its colour: *LOD*
  (blue) and *LLOQ* (purple), with a dotted line, or *LOD = LLOQ* (orange) when they are the same
  level, and *ULOQ* (olive). The ULOQ is always the actual top of the linear range: when the curve
  keeps more levels (the minimum number of calibration levels), those levels are in the olive area.
- **Above the plot**, the parameters of the curve (model, R², LOD, LLOQ, ULOQ, highest calibration
  concentration, the curve used) and notes, e.g. why a curve is not valid.
- **The title** is coloured as the row of the compound in table 4.2: red when it has no valid
  curve, orange when it was kept although not valid, blue when it uses the global curve, grey when
  it was removed before calibration.
- **Curve** (only for a compound that uses the global curve, with several batches): the calibration
  points of all batches, which the global curve was fitted on, or only those of the batch.

**How to read it**

- **Replicates should lie close together.** A level with widely spread replicates is a sign of a
  pipetting or injection problem; with the RSD% option, the LLOQ level must have an RSD% of at most 20%.
- **Samples in the white area** are within the calibration range and quantified.
- **Samples in the grey areas** are below the LLOQ (light) or the LOD (dark). Depending on the
  setting *Replace values below the LOD/LLOQ*, their concentrations are replaced (LLOQ/2 or LLOQ/4,
  open circles) or reported as *n.q.* / *n.d.*.
- **Samples in the olive area** are above the ULOQ: within the curve but above its linear range, or
  extrapolated above its highest level. Treat these values with care, or dilute and re-measure.
- **A curve far from its calibration points**, or points bending away at the top, suggests that the
  linear range is shorter than the calibration range; see the notes in table 4.2 and the option
  *Enforce linear range*.

::: {.callout-tip}
## In the app
Use the arrow keys ↑ / ↓ to step through the rows of table 4.2 and ← / → to switch the mode; the
figure follows at once. With the processing option *Log scale for calibration curve fitting*, the
figure starts with log axes, which show the low concentrations better.
:::
